elements.element: Vendor’s indemnity package includes an express duty to defend the protected parties.
elements.evidence: Array only agrees to indemnify and hold harmless. The separate infringement procedure requires the Subject Party to control the defense at its own expense and does not require Array to defend Ono.

elements.element: Vendor’s indemnity package includes an express duty to indemnify the protected parties.
elements.evidence: Section 16.2 expressly requires Array to indemnify and hold harmless the Ono Indemnitees from liabilities arising from covered Third Party Claims.

elements.element: Customer is a protected party under Vendor’s indemnity.
elements.evidence: Ono is expressly included among the Ono Indemnitees.

elements.element: Customer’s affiliates are protected parties under Vendor’s indemnity.
elements.evidence: The definition of Ono Indemnitees expressly includes Ono’s Affiliates and associated directors, officers, employees, successors, and assigns.

elements.element: Vendor’s indemnity applies to third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 16.2 applies to liabilities from Third Party Claims, and added clause (e) expressly refers to any Third Party Claim.

elements.element: Vendor’s indemnity covers claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Clause (e) covers allegations that the development, manufacture, commercialization, or use of a Product, or practice of licensed Array patents or know-how, infringes or misappropriates any third party intellectual property right.

elements.element: Vendor’s indemnity covers third-party claims arising from Vendor’s breach of law.
elements.evidence: No indemnity trigger expressly covers Array’s breach of applicable law. The reference to breaches of Article 15 representations, warranties, or covenants does not establish such coverage from the language provided.

elements.element: Vendor’s indemnity covers third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No data-breach or security-incident indemnity trigger appears.

elements.element: Vendor’s indemnity covers third-party claims arising from Vendor’s gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: The clause only excludes claims caused by an Ono Indemnitee’s gross negligence or willful misconduct; it does not affirmatively cover claims arising from Array’s gross negligence or willful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnity procedure requires prompt notice of every covered indemnity claim.
elements.evidence: Prompt written notice is required only for the defined patent Infringement Actions, not for all claims covered by Section 16.2, including other IP, breach-of-law, data-breach, or misconduct claims.

elements.element: The indemnity procedure gives Vendor control of the defense, subject to customary protections for Customer.
elements.evidence: The Subject Party, which may be Ono, controls its own defense in its sole discretion and at its own expense. Array is not given control as indemnifying party.

elements.element: The indemnity procedure requires Customer to provide reasonable cooperation in the defense.
elements.evidence: The parties must discuss strategy and the Subject Party must provide updates, but there is no operative reasonable-cooperation obligation.

elements.element: Any Customer indemnity is limited to claims arising from Customer-provided content or Customer’s breach of law.
elements.evidence: No Customer-to-Vendor indemnity appears in the rendered operative language, so no broader Customer indemnity is imposed.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Clause (e) requires Array to indemnify Ono for Third Party Claims alleging that Products or the licensed Array patents or know-how infringe or misappropriate third-party intellectual property rights.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Clause (e) excludes claims to the extent arising from Ono’s modification of a Product.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Clause (e) excludes claims arising from combining a Product with a product not supplied or approved by Array.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes infringement caused by compliance with Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: There is no exclusion for claims caused by Customer-provided designs, instructions, or specifications.

elements.element: For an infringing service or deliverable, Vendor must procure the right for Customer to continue using it.
elements.evidence: No procure-rights remedy appears.

elements.element: For an infringing service or deliverable, Vendor must modify it to become non-infringing.
elements.evidence: No modification remedy appears.

elements.element: For an infringing service or deliverable, Vendor must replace it with a non-infringing alternative.
elements.evidence: No replacement remedy appears.

elements.element: If the other IP remedies are unavailable, Vendor must refund the applicable fees.
elements.evidence: No refund remedy appears.

elements.element: Vendor’s indemnity liability is subject to a super-cap equal to three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No indemnity cap or three-times-annual-fees super-cap appears in the rendered language.

result.reason: The redline adds a substantive Vendor IP indemnity and two customary exclusions, but it omits the preferred defense duty and several preferred claim categories and procedures. It also fails the fallback because it lacks the specifications exclusion, all listed infringement remedies, and the 3× annual-fees super-cap. The addition is related to the requested allocation and does not negate the unrelated existing indemnities or the warranty disclaimer, but the Subject Party’s obligation to control the defense at its own expense creates tension with the new indemnity. Because the redline reaches neither complete position, it is not minimal to a complete accepted level.
